paper.title: RoboNeuron: A Middle-Layer Infrastructure for Agent-Driven Orchestration in Embodied AI
paper.central_claim: RoboNeuron derives MCP tools from ROS schemas, provides unified direct and persistent PIC execution, and localizes backend/runtime/acceleration changes within a stable inference boundary, enabling reusable modular robot orchestration without system rewiring.

evidence.locator: I contribution scope; fixed text line 9
evidence.quote: RoboNeuron is a middleware infrastructure that bridges agent tool calling and robot middleware, rather than a planning algorithm or a replacement for existing robot control stacks.
evidence.support_explanation: Evaluate software execution/interface claim, not invented planning superiority.

evidence.quote: The system parses ROS message definitions to resolve fields, including nested structures and arrays, and constructs a structured tool argument schema.
evidence.support_explanation: Typed schema derivation is the actual bridge mechanism.

evidence.quote: A dedicated stop tool manages process cleanup, utilizing a bounded wait period before resorting to a forced termination to maintain predictable system states.
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit runtime lifecycle, not a validated physical safety guarantee.

evidence.locator: III-C action/control contract; fixed text line 15
evidence.quote: Upon initialization, the controller parses a URDF (omitting visual and collision elements for efficiency) to build a kinematic chain, and it subscribes to both the action topic and joint-state feedback.
evidence.support_explanation: Geometry is kinematic with state feedback; collision-aware planning cannot be inferred.

evidence.quote: the agent can restart the inference module with the new configuration while the perception and control modules continue to run, ensuring the overall system topology remains intact.
evidence.support_explanation: Retained runtime topology, not retained learned improvement; restart rather than atomic seamless policy handover.

evidence.quote: Each suite contains 10 tasks, and each task is evaluated over 50 episodes.
evidence.support_explanation: LIBERO four suites supply counted closed-loop evaluation (500 episodes per suite).

evidence.locator: IV-C Table I; fixed text line 18
evidence.support_explanation: Moderate pruning has small mixed success changes and 1.17x inference speed, not universal improvement.

evidence.locator: IV-C Table I; fixed text line 18
evidence.support_explanation: Strong pruning reduces success materially; boundary preserves wiring, not behavior.

evidence.quote: The real-robot study emphasizes feasibility and runtime semantics rather than large-scale statistical performance.
evidence.support_explanation: FR3 grasping lacks counted task reliability; qualitative hardware case is not transfer evidence under the strict rule.

evidence.locator: IV-A separate experiments; fixed text line 18
evidence.quote: This design separates task-level comparison under a fixed serving setup from inference-level efficiency comparison under runtime-augmented configurations, while keeping the external observation/action contract unchanged.
evidence.support_explanation: Do not combine two distinct VLA studies into a joint speed-and-success result.

evidence.quote: Our current implementation focuses on message-level exposure via topics, which addresses the low-latency primitives required for our evaluation.
evidence.support_explanation: Broader ROS service/action coverage is not demonstrated.

signatures.object: ROS capability to external agent tool
signatures.information: Robot message schemas and configured topic endpoints; external frozen agent sees typed tools, not an embedded planner
signatures.operation: Parse nested/array fields, build typed validation schema, recursively encode validated arguments and publish ROS messages
signatures.output: Discoverable MCP tool, one-shot commands or timed sequences
signatures.conditions: Correct topic/schema binding and robot-side command semantics; syntactic validation does not establish physical feasibility
signatures.feedback: Tool/runtime state available to external agent; no independent task-success verifier implemented
signatures.selection_rule: Static deterministic schema validation and configured endpoints
signatures.later_use: Reused invocations/robots through configured bindings, not retained autonomous learning
signatures.claimed_effect: Less manual wrapper drift and integration work
signatures.failure_boundary: Only topic/message exposure; no measured schema-evolution or maintenance-effort benchmark

signatures.object: Persistent PIC execution and backend switching
signatures.information: Camera images/instructions to selected frozen VLA; action delta plus gripper to controller; current joints and URDF to IK
signatures.operation: Spawn isolated ROS2 processes, stream perception/inference/control; stop/restart inference under unchanged topics
signatures.output: Joint commands, explicit bounded lifecycle and selectable runtime/pruning presets
signatures.conditions: Backends obey fixed 6-DoF delta/gripper semantics; process termination and restart safe for robot state
signatures.feedback: Joint feedback closes controller; external agent monitors progress; no newly trained state persists
signatures.selection_rule: Agent/config selects backend/preset; no automatic performance-based accept/reject protocol
signatures.selection_data: LIBERO evaluates choices but not an online selector
signatures.persistence: Static modules/configurations and current running processes only
signatures.later_use: Same communication topology after restart; no measured later-task learning
signatures.claimed_effect: Topology-preserving orchestration and controlled backend comparison
signatures.failure_boundary: URDF collision elements omitted; action semantic equivalence, reset/switch hazards and long-running reliability unquantified

gap.author_gap: Ad hoc agent wrappers drift from robot schemas; persistent execution and changing VLA/serving backends require repeated integration.
gap.checked_gap: Specific reusable runtime seam between MCP tool calls and ROS streaming is credible. Paper distinguishes its middleware claim from planning algorithms, but does not quantify engineering costs saved.

lineage.relation: ROS2/MoveIt/Nav2/OpenRTM supply modular robot software; SayCan/Code as Policies/ProgPrompt target reasoning rather than bridge maintenance.

closest_adjacent.source: ROS2mcpserver and ROS2mcp, as described in II
closest_adjacent.version: Neighbor originals not fixed in packet
closest_adjacent.limitation: Only paper's comparison of protocol bridge versus schema/lifecycle reuse is available; no independent exhaustive novelty claim.

gap.residue: Schema-aligned exposure plus explicit persistent lifecycle and replaceable inference boundary under common topic contracts.
gap.stakes: Integration and attribution costs matter to robot experimentation, but developer time/drift reduction is not measured.
gap.method_response: Deterministic schema derivation, control/data-plane separation, direct/PIC workflows and inference-only restart.
gap.remaining_gap: Lifecycle reliability under faults, agent-level task success/false completion, service/action coverage, quantitative maintenance benefit and multiple-hardware switching trials.
unresolved: Novelty-critical adjacent original sources would require common fixed supplementation for both seats.

candidate_checks.reason: Full card read. Common tool schema is a software protocol, not mapping modalities into one uniform model/objective. Bespoke VLA wrappers/controllers remain; C18 steps 2-3 and its semantic shared-substrate validation do not apply.

Full cards read. Modularity and typed dispatch alone do not implement the solver/check/revise tactic; no external result-validity loop into LLM artifact revision. Middleware is the contribution rather than comparative-advantage reasoning decomposition.

rs_pattern.reason: Useful runtime infrastructure without a justified exact original 15+31 operation; do not stretch 'unify' to generic API standardization.

condition_checks.reason: Schemas generated from nested ROS messages and bound publishers.
Direct/PIC share tools; bounded stop and inference restart preserve topic wiring.
Counted LIBERO moderate presets retain similar success, but no unpruned RN row, and P75 harms outcomes.
Qualitative agent/hardware cases, no end-to-end completion denominator or audited false completion.

failure_checks: R04's qualitative-agent and aggressive-pruning failure conditions apply; schema validation is not physical safety.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Exact domain operation is exposing ROS and policy lifecycle as typed MCP tools; no original-taxonomy match asserted.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: Stable syntactic and action contracts assumed; protocol uniformity does not guarantee safe agent choices or behavior-equivalent backends.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; paper-practice/limitation synthesis, not actual reviewer comments
expectations.applies_when: Middleware contribution claimed to improve agent orchestration
expectations.reason: Same VLA harness in LIBERO shows feasibility; no same-agent alternate middleware task-success or developer-effort comparison.
Pruning variants held within fixed topology; baseline to RN+pruning confounds wrapper and preset. No schema/lifecycle removal test.
500 episodes per suite, but no seed repeats/intervals or task-paired uncertainty for subpercentage gains.
Normalized inference speed and hardware provided; no end-to-end agent tokens/time/failure cost or measured engineering effort. Latency and task studies differ.
FR3 case intentionally feasibility-only without counted trials.
No retained self-improvement claim; static infrastructure evaluated as such.

claims.text: Unified reusable tool/PIC interface and switching without rewiring
claims.setting: Multi-base and single-arm simulation; FR3 grasping; OpenVLA/OFT/pi0 supported
claims.baseline/control: Paper-described ad hoc wrappers and existing ROS-MCP bridges, no direct empirical maintenance control
claims.selection_vs_test: Mechanism case studies; no development/holdout schema-evolution partition
claims.budget: Runtime configuration and common streams; case-level call/attempt counts absent
claims.result/denominator: Architectural algorithms and qualitative execution sequences; no agent-task success denominator
claims.failures: Fault/switch stress reliability and false completion not counted
counterevidence: Code-level architecture supports mechanism feasibility, not quantified savings or general reliable orchestration
claims.allowed_conclusion: Authors describe and demonstrate a coherent schema/lifecycle infrastructure, with broad effectiveness not causally measured.

claims.text: Backend-side changes under fixed topology can preserve success and accelerate inference
claims.setting: LIBERO four suites, 10 tasks each, 50 episodes/task; separate OpenVLA RTX4090 latency study
claims.baseline/control: OpenVLA-OFT baseline versus RN+P25/P50/P75; pruning presets otherwise fixed serving
claims.selection_vs_test: Standard benchmark evaluation, no disclosure of tuning/development overlap
claims.budget: Same evaluation topology; inference speed normalized, end-to-end resource use absent
claims.failures: Aggressive pruning performance loss, no per-task failure taxonomy
counterevidence: No unpruned RN success row; task-success and runtime-enhanced latency studies are separate
claims.allowed_conclusion: Moderate preset feasibility and an explicit speed/quality tradeoff, not agent-level superiority or universally free swapping.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported counted LIBERO closed-loop results support compatible topology-preserving inference variations; qualitative simulation/FR3 cases demonstrate orchestration feasibility. They do not measure engineering savings, safe lifecycle reliability or end-to-end LLM-agent success, and uncounted hardware cases do not qualify as transfer.

X.reason: Static operation, input/action contract and explicit process lifecycle reconstructable; only topic exposure, no fault/lifecycle semantic audit or quantified cross-backend equivalence.

causality.reason: Fixed topology controls preset variation, but no pure RN/unpruned comparison or schema/lifecycle alternative baseline; cannot attribute success differences or saved engineering work to middleware.

holdout.reason: Four standard suites offer task variety, but development/preset selection overlap unreported; qualitative cross-platform cases do not establish independent reliability transfer.
